gates.headline: 30 exact rational identities; 30/30 mutations rejected
gates.registered_claim: Theorem 4.4 gives a closed-form reduction of the privacy loss distribution (PLD) of k-out-of-t random allocation to t-wise convolutions of exponentiated PLD terms (Section 4, Theorem 4.4).

gates.headline: 17 fast/exact cases, 6 released API cases, α⁻² scaling
gates.registered_claim: The proposed algorithm computes an (α,β)-accurate approximation of the random allocation PLD in time O(log³(t)·log(t/β)/α²), using exponentiation-by-squaring with geometric-grid rounding (Section 4, Theorem 4.6).

gates.headline: 24 exact φ_λ identities; 24/24 mutations rejected
gates.registered_claim: Theorem 3.3 introduces transformation rules φ_λ that apply Poisson subsampling directly to PLD realizations, allowing subsampling and random allocation to be composed within one unified PLD framework (Section 3, Theorem 3.3, Definition 3.1).

gates.headline: t={1000,10000}, δ=10⁻⁶; PLD<RDP at 20/20 points; independent Chua and Monte Carlo checks
gates.registered_claim: Numerical experiments show the new random allocation privacy bounds are nearly identical to the Monte Carlo lower bounds of Chua et al. (2024a) and substantially tighter than RDP-based analytic bounds, for t ∈ {1000, 10000} and δ = 10⁻⁶ (Section 5, Figures 1-2).

gates.headline: n=1000, δ=10⁻¹⁰; allocation requires less noise in 3/3 panels; locator is literally false
gates.literal_falsification: The Bernoulli experiment is Figure 5 in the paper, not the registered Figure 4.
gates.registered_claim: A toy Bernoulli mean-estimation experiment (n=10³, δ=10⁻¹⁰) shows random allocation requires strictly lower noise than Poisson subsampling for the same privacy level, demonstrating a genuine privacy (not just variance) advantage (Section 5, Figure 4).

gates.headline: exact n,d,C,E constants; PLD<RDP at 40/40 points; locator is literally false
gates.literal_falsification: The PREAMBLE comparison is Figure 3 in the paper, not the registered Figure 5.
gates.registered_claim: Applied to a DP-SGD scenario with block-sparse coordinate sampling (n=6×10⁵, d=2²⁰, C=2¹⁵, E=10 epochs), the PLD accounting method improves privacy bounds over RDP composition even under heavy composition (Section 5, Figure 5).

paper.title: Efficient privacy loss accounting for subsampling and random allocation
